title: Operatorize EKS control-plane Terraform module for safer upgrades and preflight checks
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Refactor the existing EKS control-plane Terraform code into an operator-friendly, idempotent module that supports safe rolling/ canary upgrades and automatic preflight checks. Deliverables include: a modular Terraform interface (inputs/outputs) suitable for both Hosted and Private deployments; lifecycle hooks for pre-upgrade validation and post-upgrade verification; an on-change plan dry-run that can be surfaced in PRs; lightweight canary/gradual rollout flags and a rollback automation pattern; metric and health probe exports for Console dashboards; and documentation + CI jobs that enforce idempotent plans. This work is targeted at reducing upgrade toil, avoiding noisy rollbacks, and making private cluster upgrades observable and reversible with low blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Module compiles and passes terraform plan/apply in a clean account with documented inputs
Preflight step runs automatically in CI and fails builds when plan contains destructive changes to control-plane nodes without approval
Canary rollout flag can target a single AZ or nodegroup and rollback is automatable via documented runbook
Prometheus metrics and a basic health-check exporter are emitted to CloudWatch/Prometheus for Console dashboards
Upgrade path tested end-to-end in staging: plan -> canary -> gradual -> full with metrics/alerts verifying no regressions
All existing Private deployment tests (idempotency, drift detection) pass and module supports zero-downtime upgrades for minor version bumps
steps: Audit current control-plane Terraform code and extract reusable primitives (kms, nodegroups, iam, eks addons)
Design operatorized inputs: explicit version pinning, canary selectors, preflight toggles, rollout policies
Implement lifecycle hooks: preflight (dry-run + static checks), pre-upgrade snapshotting, post-upgrade verification
Add observability: lightweight exporter that publishes control-plane health and nodegroup rollout progress
Create CI pipeline: terraform fmt/checks, plan with diff comment to PR, automatic preflight gate
Implement canary mechanism: terraform variables and tagging to isolate target AZ/nodegroup; rollback automation via documented steps and helper scripts
Document module usage and runbooks; include migration guide from legacy provisioner
Run staging upgrade exercise and capture postmortem
notes: We intentionally avoid heavy operator runtime (e.g., Kubernetes operator) to keep lifecycle in Terraform and runtime minimal; tradeoff is some orchestration logic in CI and runbooks
Plan to reuse existing KMS cross-account patterns but reduce secret sprawl by pinning KMS aliases and documenting IAM expectations
Rollback design prefers automated DNS/traffic shift when possible but otherwise falls back to Terraform-based revert and recreates snapshots for quick rollback
